issues.legal_issue: A court order modifying an award in a statutory arbitration governed by the general arbitration framework is appealable under the framework’s appeal provisions.
material_facts: A title dispute arising during consolidation proceedings was referred through the Civil Judge to an arbitrator appointed under the consolidation law.
The arbitrator submitted an award to the Civil Court, and objections were filed against it.
The Civil Judge modified the award, and the District Court entertained an appeal from that modification.
The governing consolidation law provided for arbitration and applied the general arbitration law to the proceedings, subject to specified exceptions.
issues.conclusion: The Civil Judge’s decision modifying the award was appealable under section 39 of the Arbitration Act, 1940.
issues.legal_principle: Section 37 of the Uttar Pradesh Consolidation of Holdings Act provided for appointment of the arbitrator and required the matter in other respects to be determined under the Arbitration Act. Read with sections 46 and 47 of the Arbitration Act, that applied sections 15 and 39 to the statutory arbitration. The finality provision in section 12(6) of the Uttar Pradesh Act made final the arbitrator’s decision as it emerged after any appropriate proceedings under the Arbitration Act. Sarju Prasad v. Civil Judge, Farrukhabad and Sayed Ullah Khan v. The Temporary Civil Judge, Sultanpur were approved. Attar Singh v. State of U.P. was explained as not deciding whether section 39 applied.

predicates.statutory_arbitration: A dispute was referred to an arbitrator under a statutory process.
predicates.general_arbitration_framework_applies: The governing statutory process requires the general arbitration framework to apply to the arbitration proceedings beyond the appointment of the arbitrator.
predicates.court_modified_award: A court modified an arbitrator’s award.

issues.definition: When a dispute is referred to an arbitrator under a statutory process, the general arbitration framework applies, and a court modifies the award, the modification order is appealable.
